$comment: RFC 0155 §C — versioned extension registry.
Closed records for the normative extensions this corpus defines. `maturity` is
one of experimental|draft|stable|deprecated, and §C sets a hard bar for stable:
normative prose, schemas, non-vacuous conformance, SDK support where applicable,
and at least one Tier-3 implementation.
BACKFILL 2026-08-16 (RFC 0155 UQ3 — grandfathering). Every optional capability
family in `schemas/capabilities.schema.json` now has a record; the derived
`coverage` block partitions the family set into core-predicate fields, discovery
METADATA (keys that describe the document/host rather than gate a feature —
each with a stated rationale), covered, and uncovered, and `--check` fails if a
family arrives in none of them. Grandfathering rule: an extension whose owning
RFC is `Active`/`Accepted`, or whose home is a v1 base spec document, enters at
`draft`; one whose owning RFC is `Draft`/`Parked` enters at `experimental`.
Nothing enters at `stable` — see the ceiling below.
Fields beyond the §C example: `owningDoc` (spec/v1/*.md) names the normative
home when the family predates the RFC process (`owningRfc: null` — six v1 base
advertisements: secrets, webhooks, i18n, aiProviders, envelopeContracts,
envelopeStrictness); `securityTier` is high|medium|low — high when the family
reaches credentials, tenant-isolated storage, egress, sandboxing, or
authorization; `minimumSuiteVersion` is DERIVED as the suite version at which
the named scenario witness first landed (`git log --diff-filter=A` on the file →
conformance/package.json at that commit), null when no scenario reads the family
(a stated suite gap, not a pass); `note` names the witness and the RFC status.
NOTE: every record here is at most `draft`. §C gates `stable` on a Tier-3
implementation, and no Tier-3 host exists — the `ROADMAP.md` tripwire has not
fired. That ceiling is a fact about adoption, not about the maturity of the work,
and the registry states it instead of quietly promoting anything. `evidenceTier`
is therefore null on every record; tier-1/tier-2 execution evidence lives in
INTEROP-MATRIX.md and the hosts' certification bundles, not here.

coverage.rule: Derived by scripts/generate-extension-registry-coverage.mjs from the top-level keys of schemas/capabilities.schema.json. coreFields = the openwop-discovery-core predicate fields (profiles.md); metadataFields = keys that describe the document or host rather than gate an optional feature (each carries its rationale in metadataRationale; a key that gates behaviour may not be listed there); covered = extension families reached by some record capabilityPath; uncovered = every other family. Uncovered means no registry record exists — not that the family is non-compliant. Regenerate with --write; the gate runs --check.

metadataRationale.compliance: which masking mode is in effect (closes O5) — describes an operator setting so clients can read `[REDACTED]` correctly
metadataRationale.configurable: per-run `RunOptions.configurable` overlay keys the server honours; a schema hint
metadataRationale.conformance: conformance-only typeIds the host registered (RFC 0023) — evidence apparatus, not a feature
metadataRationale.discovery: discovery-change-detection advertisement (capabilities-change-detection.md) — describes the discovery document itself
metadataRationale.engineVersion: server engine version axis (version-negotiation.md); a number, not a feature
metadataRationale.extensions: per-canvas / per-workflow overrides (additional envelope types, override limits); an override slot, not a family
metadataRationale.fixtures: fixture workflow ids the host seeded — a hint to the suite about what it may drive
metadataRationale.minClientVersion: minimum SDK version the server interops with; a pin, not a feature
metadataRationale.protocolVersions: RFC 0165 §A — every protocol major.minor the host serves; a version advertisement beside `protocolVersion`, not a capability family.
metadataRationale.runtimeCapabilities: opaque ids NodeModules may `requires`; a vocabulary the host names, not a contract this corpus defines
metadataRationale.supportedTransports: transport list; REST is required regardless and gRPC has its own `grpc` family
metadataRationale.testing: testing-mode advertisement (mock providers, seams) — for suites and dev clients, not a production feature
